question: A newlywed couple comes to your office for genetic counseling. Both potential parents are known to be carriers of the same Cystic Fibrosis (CF) mutation. What is the probability that at least one of their next three children will have CF if they are all single births?
analysis: When both parents are carriers of the same CF mutation, there is a 25% chance with each pregnancy that the child will have CF. The probability of at least one of their next three children having CF can be calculated using the complement rule, which is 1 minus the probability of none of the children having CF. Therefore, the probability is 1 - (3/4)^3 = 37/64.
